title: Pipe Sizing Fundamentals: Trunk and Branch Balance
description: Undersized water supply lines are one of the primary causes of severe pressure drop when multiple fixtures run at the same time. Plumbing supply systems rely on a balance between pipe diameter, flow rate, and friction loss. Using a larger main trunk line—such as 3/4-inch—to supply smaller 1/2-inch fixture branches maintains adequate water volume throughout the system. Undersizing main supply pipes forces water through at excessively high velocities, causing noisy operation, pipe erosion, and weak shower pressure. Sizing must always align with total Water Supply Fixture Units (WSFU) calculated under your local plumbing code. What pipe sizes do you typically see used for main supply trunks in your area?

High detail, photorealistic visual, physically accurate plumbing fittings, no text, no visual labels, no watermarks, no logos.
visual_story: The visual demonstrates the fundamental physical transition from a main water distribution pipe to smaller branch lines. By showing a detailed internal cutaway of the pipe wall and fittings, the viewer can immediately see how internal pipe diameter directly governs available water volume before it reaches individual fixtures.

on_image_text.hook: Why Water Pressure Drops When Two Taps Run
on_image_text.explanation: Undersized supply lines restrict total water volume, causing severe pressure drop across simultaneous fixtures.
on_image_text.takeaway: Size main supply lines for total fixture demand, not just single-tap convenience.
